Tom Brady. An American football quarterback widely regarded as the greatest to ever play the position. Drafted one hundred ninety-ninth overall in the sixth round in 2000 by the New England Patriots after a relatively unheralded college career at Michigan, he led the franchise to six Super Bowl victories and redefined the quarterback position through longevity, precision passing, and competitive excellence spanning nearly twenty-three seasons. He won six Super Bowl championships, five with New England and one with Tampa Bay, appearing in nine total championships, more than any player in NFL history. He spent twenty seasons with the Patriots from 2000 to 2019, winning four Super Bowl titles and numerous AFC East division championships. He earned fifteen Pro Bowl selections and won three Super Bowl MVP awards, establishing himself as the league's most decorated playoff performer. He threw over six hundred touchdown passes and eighty thousand career passing yards, ranking among the all-time leaders in both categories. He played until age forty-five, the oldest starting quarterback in NFL history, demonstrating unprecedented longevity and physical durability. He joined the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020 and led them to a Super Bowl championship in his first season.
